text: As per my last email, the deadline was Friday. I'm not sure what happened.
annotation_notes: Explicit reference to prior communication implies the recipient failed to read it

text: Thanks for finally getting that done. No worries, I'm sure you were busy.
annotation_notes: Finally implies lateness; I'm sure you were busy is a sarcastic excuse

text: Fine. Do whatever you want.
annotation_notes: Fine as a curt reply signals disengagement; context affects certainty

text: I disagree with your approach — here's why.
annotation_notes: Direct clear disagreement with reasoning — no hidden hostility

text: You are completely useless.
annotation_notes: Direct personal attack — no indirection

text: With all due respect, I think you're missing the point.
annotation_notes: With all due respect is a common mock-politeness marker; depends on tone and relationship

text: Not to be rude, but that presentation was a disaster.
annotation_notes: Not to be rude but precedes an explicitly critical statement — indirect hostility

text: That was hilarious 😂
annotation_notes: Genuine amusement — not sarcastic in isolation; no hostile target

text: Could you send me the report by end of day?
annotation_notes: Direct polite request — no hostility indicators

text: Sorry you feel that way.
annotation_notes: Classic dismissive phrase — acknowledges feelings without taking any responsibility

text: I just assumed you'd handle it since you always do.
annotation_notes: Since you always do is a backhanded compliment; combined with assumed implies guilt

text: Stop wasting everyone's time with these ideas.
annotation_notes: Direct dismissal and attack on the person's contributions

text: No worries!
annotation_notes: Standalone no worries is ambiguous — could be genuine reassurance or passive-aggressive; context required

text: I'm frustrated by the delays but I understand things come up.
annotation_notes: Direct expression of emotion with acknowledgment — not passive aggressive

text: Wow great job on the report... it only took three weeks.
annotation_notes: Ellipsis and only took three weeks are clear sarcastic signals targeting the recipient

text: I can't believe how incompetent you are.
annotation_notes: Direct personal attack using incompetent label

text: Whatever you think is best.
annotation_notes: Feigned deference masking disengagement; highly context-dependent

text: I already mentioned this in yesterday's meeting.
annotation_notes: Implies the recipient did not pay attention — redirects blame

text: Thank you for your feedback.
annotation_notes: Could be genuine or dismissive; context needed — default neutral

text: I don't think this will work because of X Y and Z.
annotation_notes: Clear direct analytical disagreement with reasons

text: I guess I'll just do it myself then.
annotation_notes: Implies the recipient has failed to help; designed to induce guilt

text: Bless your heart.
annotation_notes: Southern US phrase often used to condescend while appearing polite; context dependent

text: I'm sure you were very busy with more important things.
annotation_notes: Sarcastic implication that the recipient prioritized other tasks over this person

text: Oh really. How interesting.
annotation_notes: Flat delivery implied by context; sarcastic dismissal

text: I've been waiting two weeks for this.
annotation_notes: Stating wait time without context is a guilt-tripping signal

text: The project was delivered on time and meets all requirements.
annotation_notes: Factual status update — no hostility

text: Not that it matters, but I finished my part last week.
annotation_notes: Not that it matters but raises something intended to matter; combined with finished early implies the recipient is behind

text: Honestly I'm surprised you managed to finish.
annotation_notes: Expressed surprise at a task completion implies low prior expectation

text: At least you tried.
annotation_notes: Classic backhanded consolation that implies failure

text: Better late than never!
annotation_notes: Common phrase used to highlight lateness while appearing positive

text: I'm not angry. I'm just disappointed.
annotation_notes: Classic guilt-trip formula; disappointment framed to impose emotional burden

text: Sure, if you think that's the right approach.
annotation_notes: Feigned agreement while clearly skeptical; context dependent on tone

text: Could we schedule a call to discuss this further?
annotation_notes: Direct professional request

text: Oh GREAT. Now we have to redo everything.
annotation_notes: Caps on GREAT signals strong sarcasm; redo everything is an explicit complaint rather than indirect

text: I expected better from you.
annotation_notes: Direct statement of negative expectation targeting the person

text: Do whatever you want. I'm done.
annotation_notes: Combination of disengagement and implied consequence

text: As I've mentioned multiple times already...
annotation_notes: Multiple times already is a blame-shift emphasizing recipient inattention

text: That's certainly one way to look at it.
annotation_notes: Dismissive validation that implies the view is wrong without stating it

text: Good for you.
annotation_notes: Often used sarcastically to dismiss someone's achievement

text: I'm glad we could clear that up.
annotation_notes: Could be genuine closure or passive-aggressive; default neutral without context

text: You never take anything seriously.
annotation_notes: Direct sweeping criticism using never

text: No worries, I'll handle it. Like I always do.
annotation_notes: Like I always do is a clear guilt-tripping addition implying habitual unfair burden

text: I just want to make sure we're on the same page.
annotation_notes: Direct clarification request — no hostility

text: Well, that's just your opinion.
annotation_notes: Dismissive deflection of a point without engaging with it

text: I can't work with someone who doesn't listen.
annotation_notes: Direct statement of inability to work with the person

text: Thanks in advance!
annotation_notes: Thanks in advance is very common and often genuinely polite; only PA if demanding tone — default neutral

text: I'm sure you have your reasons.
annotation_notes: Dismissive implied sarcasm — I'm sure signals doubt

text: Your work on this has been outstanding.
annotation_notes: Straightforward positive assessment — no backhanded elements

text: Must be nice to have so much free time.
annotation_notes: Implicit accusation that the recipient is not working while the speaker is overburdened

text: The deadline is tomorrow. Please have it ready.
annotation_notes: Direct reminder with no indirection or hostility
